entities.name: Antoine Bohier Du Prat
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Antoine Bohier Du Prat (d. 1519) emerged as a pivotal figure in early 16th-century France, serving as Archbishop of Bourges and, critically, as Chancellor of France under King Francis I. His career spanned the transition from the late Medieval to the early Renaissance, a period marked by intense negotiations between the French monarchy and the Papacy over ecclesiastical control. Bohier played a central role in articulating and advancing the Gallican liberties, seeking to define the autonomy of the French church from direct Roman intervention, a struggle that profoundly shaped the political and religious landscape of Western Europe.

Appointed Archbishop of Bourges in 1514 and elevated to cardinal in 1517, Bohier Du Prat's most enduring contribution was his instrumental involvement in the negotiation and implementation of the Concordat of Bologna in 1516. This landmark agreement, signed between Francis I and Pope Leo X, effectively abrogated the Pragmatic Sanction of Bourges (1438) and granted the French king the right to nominate bishops, abbots, and other high ecclesiastical officials within his realm. Bohier's legal acumen and diplomatic skill were crucial in securing terms that significantly enhanced royal power over the French church's extensive wealth and personnel, centralizing authority previously contested by cathedral chapters and monastic communities.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Antoine Bohier Du Prat played a pivotal role in negotiating the Concordat of Bologna (1516), which fundamentally reshaped the relationship between the French monarchy and the Papacy, granting French kings significant control over the national church for centuries. His actions had a lasting impact on French state-building and religious autonomy.
